planting.note: Plant divisions or lab-propagated starts in fall into moist, humus- and lime-rich soil in partial shade; like all Cypripedium it is slow to establish and depends on mycorrhizal fungi in the root zone, so avoid disturbing settled plants.

directions: Chinese yellow lady's slipper is a terrestrial slipper orchid native to open forest edges and grassy slopes in the mountains of Gansu, Hubei, Sichuan, Yunnan, and Tibet, where it grows in moist, alkaline soil at high elevation. In late spring it produces one or two clear yellow, pouch-shaped flowers often marked with fine red spotting inside the lip, held above a short stem of broad, pleated leaves. It is one of the two species parents (with C. macranthos) behind the easier garden hybrid Cypripedium 'Gisela,' valued for passing on good vigor. Give it humus- and lime-rich, consistently moist but well-drained soil in partial shade, and resist the urge to divide or move it often, since Cypripedium roots are slow to recover from disturbance.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; East Asian Calanthe species like this one benefit from a winter mulch where grown near the cold edge of their hardiness range.

directions: Furcate calanthe is a terrestrial East Asian woodland orchid bearing white flowers with a deeply lobed lip and a distinctive hairy, forked nectar spur, the feature that gives the species its name. It is historically significant as the white-flowered parent of Calanthe x dominyi, the cross with C. masuca that produced the first artificial orchid hybrid ever raised to bloom, in 1856. Grow it in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade beneath open woodland canopy, mimicking the dappled light of its native forest floor habitat. Divide congested clumps after flowering to propagate or to keep plantings from overcrowding.
sources: Epic Gardening -- history of Calanthe x dominyi

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring into moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; native to temperate forest at 400-1,500 m elevation across South and Southeast Asia, it tolerates both warm and cool conditions once established.

directions: Masuca calanthe is a terrestrial woodland orchid native from Sri Lanka, India, and Nepal east through Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam, southern China, and into Malaysia and Indonesia, where small conical pseudobulbs and broadly elliptic leaves support a late-summer to early-fall spike of 10 to 15 violet-lilac flowers with a deep purple lip. It supplied the violet-lilac color and deeply lobed lip to Calanthe x dominyi, the 1856 cross with C. furcata that produced the first artificial orchid hybrid ever raised to flower. Grow in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in shade to partial shade, and divide congested clumps after flowering to propagate.
